question: Enterobacteriaceae:

options.opa: They are mobile bacteria with polar flagellation.
options.opd: They do not include plant pathogens.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Enterobacteriaceae" -> "facultative anaerobes" -> "can use nitrates as electron acceptors" -> "can breathe nitrates" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Enterobacteriaceae" -> "include some plant pathogens" -> "do not exclude plant pathogens" -> 80%
analysis: Enterobacteriaceae is a large family of Gram-negative bacteria that includes many well-known pathogens. They are facultative anaerobes, meaning they can use oxygen when it is available but can also switch to anaerobic respiration. One of their characteristics is the ability to reduce nitrates to nitrites, which aligns with option opb. They are typically catalase positive, which rules out option opc. They are not known for polar flagellation, as they usually have peritrichous flagella, which rules out option opa. Additionally, some members of Enterobacteriaceae can be plant pathogens, which rules out option opd.
